title: An Adaptive Parent-mediated Intervention to Improve Outcomes for Autistic Children
official: An Adaptive Parent-mediated Intervention to Improve Outcomes for Autistic Children
summary: High quality early intervention offers significant benefits for autistic children, yet most programs fail to adjust the level of support needed to sustain parent engagement and maximize efficacy. We will utilize a Sequential Multiple Assignment Randomized Trial (SMART) trial, an implementation research design in which participants are re-randomized at key decision points, to explore methods to improve engagement in OPT-In-Early (Online Parent Training in Early Behavioral Intervention). OPT-In-Early is a self-directed online autism parent-training program that teaches evidence-based behavioral/developmental strategies to promote child skill development and reduce interfering behaviors. In this adaptive intervention, parents will first be randomized to either OPT-In-Early or OPT-In-Early with automated support. We will monitor progress and intervene early (during Month 1 of the 6-month intervention) to identify parents who either (1) demonstrate low engagement with the program or (2) use the program but do not learn information. These parents needing extra support will then be re-randomized to receive additional remote clinical support, either in the form of group or individual intervention. The intervention will be based on OPT-In-Early principles. An adaptive approach to OPT-In-Early may improve child outcomes while using resources more judiciously.

interventions.name: Online Parent Training in Early Behavioral Intervention (OPT-In-Early)

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Child age 14 to 48 months with a medical diagnosis and/or educational label of autism
* Caregiver (a) 18 years or older, (b) fluent in English or Spanish, (c) has physical custody of the child (at least 50% of the time)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Child (a) has severe hearing and/or vision impairment that is uncorrected with aids, (b) is not yet walking, (c) is receiving more than 20 hours of intervention per week at baseline
* Caregiver is receiving weekly autism-related parent coaching
